title: How to Set Up Payroll for a New Company in India
summary: A step-by-step guide on how to set up payroll for new companies in India, from registering for PF and ESI to building salary structures, configuring TDS, and running your first payroll. Also learn Razorpay Payroll handles the payroll setup for new business in India
body_markdown:
Setting up payroll for a new company in India involves more than calculating salaries and transferring money. It requires statutory registrations, salary structure decisions, TDS configuration, and a process that can run reliably every month as the team grows. Getting it right at the start is considerably easier than correcting errors after six months of payroll have been processed.


This guide walks through how to set up payroll in India for a new company, from the first statutory registrations to running a first payroll cycle, with the decisions that affect compliance and employee experience along the way.


## **What Payroll Setup Involves for a New Company**


Payroll setup for a new company in India covers six areas:


#


Area


What it involves


**1** **Statutory registrations** Registering with EPFO, ESIC, the state PT authority, and the income tax department for TDS


**2** **Salary structure design** Defining how each employee’s CTC breaks into components: basic, HRA, allowances and variable pay


**3** **Employee data collection** Gathering PAN, bank details, Aadhaar, declaration forms, and investment proofs from each employee


**4** **TDS configuration** Setting up tax regime choices, projecting annual taxable income, and computing monthly TDS for each employee


**5** **Payroll system setup** Configuring your payroll software with salary structures, compliance details, leave policies, and attendance inputs


**6** **First payroll run** Processing salaries, verifying outputs, disbursing to bank accounts, and filing the first statutory returns


Each area needs to be in place before the first payroll run. Missing a registration or skipping a configuration step creates a compliance gap from the first month that takes time and cost to correct.


## **Step 1: Register Your Company for Statutory Compliance**


Statutory registrations come first. The obligations that apply depend on your employee headcount and their gross salary levels, but most new companies will need all four.


### **Register for PF (EPFO)**


PF registration under the Code on Social Security, 2020 is mandatory for any establishment with 20 or more employees. Many companies register voluntarily before hitting that threshold.

### **Register for ESI (ESIC)**


ESI registration under the Code on Social Security, 2020 is mandatory for establishments with 10 or more employees where employees earn ₹21,000 or less per month in gross salary.

Register under the state PT legislation for each state where you have employees. The registration, an Employer Registration Certificate (ERC), is issued by the state tax authority. PT applies based on each employee’s work location, not your company’s registered office.


### **Register for TDS (TAN)**


Every employer that deducts tax at source from salaries must hold a Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number (TAN). Apply online on the Protean portal (formerly NSDL e-Gov) using Form 135 (previously Form 49B), or along with your company’s incorporation on the MCA portal. The application needs your company’s PAN and CIN, the name and PAN of the person responsible for deducting tax, and proof of identity, address and date of incorporation.


TAN is used for all TDS payments and returns: quarterly Form 138 (previously 24Q) for salary TDS and Form 140 (previously 26Q) for non-salary payments such as professional fees.


## **Step 2: Build Your Salary Structure**


The salary structure determines how each employee’s Cost to Company (CTC) breaks into components. This decision affects take-home pay, tax liability, and PF contributions, so it is worth thinking through before the first payroll run rather than after.


Component


What it is


Payroll implication


**Basic salary** Fixed core component, typically 40–50% of CTC


PF is calculated on PF wages: basic and DA, plus any excluded allowances above 50% of total compensation, up to the ₹25,000 ceiling


**HRA (House Rent Allowance)** Allowance for rent; partially tax-exempt if the employee lives in rented accommodation


Exempt under Schedule III, S. No. 11 (previously Section 10(13A)) subject to conditions; reduces TDS for eligible employees


**Special allowance** Balance component after other allowances; fully taxable


No exemptions; included in taxable income for TDS computation


**LTA (Leave Travel Allowance)** Travel allowance, tax-exempt on submission of travel bills twice in a four-year block


Reduces TDS when employee submits valid LTA claims; unclaimed LTA is fully taxable


**Variable pay / performance bonus** Performance-linked component, paid quarterly or annually


Fully taxable; triggers TDS recalculation when paid; not part of monthly guaranteed CTC


**Employer PF contribution** 12% of applicable PF wages paid by employer


Part of CTC; not in employee’s gross salary but a payroll cost for the company


The New Labour Codes, in effect since November 2025, changed how wages are defined for PF, gratuity and statutory bonus. Under the Codes, the wage component must be at least 50% of total compensation for most employees, so check your component ratios when you build your first salary structure. ## **Step 3: Collect Employee Information**


Before payroll can run, you need the following from each employee:


- **PAN:** required for TDS computation and Form 130 (previously Form 16) issuance; without PAN, TDS is deducted at 20%


- **Bank account details:** account number, IFSC code, and account holder name for salary disbursal


- **Aadhaar-linked UAN:** Universal Account Number for PF. Employees who have contributed to PF before will have an existing UAN; new entrants get one on first registration


- **Tax regime choice:** whether the employee opts for the old regime (the new regime applies by default)


- **Investment declaration (Form 124, previously Form 12BB):** under the old regime, claims for HRA, LTA and deductions such as Section 123 (previously 80C), used to compute projected TDS


- **Work location:** determines PT applicability, slab, and state-level LWF


Employee self-onboarding, where each hire fills in their own details directly in the payroll system, removes the manual data entry step and reduces entry errors. It also gives each employee a record of what they submitted.


## **Step 4: Configure TDS for Each Employee**


TDS on salary is a projection. At the start of the financial year (or on joining), each employee’s annual taxable income is estimated based on their salary structure and declared investments, and the resulting tax is divided into equal monthly deductions across the remaining months.


The key inputs to TDS configuration:


- **Gross annual salary** from the salary structure


- **Tax regime** (old or new): employees choose at the start of the year; default is the new regime under current rules


- **Standard deduction** : ₹75,000 under the new regime from FY 2024-25


- **HRA and LTA exemptions** : applicable only under the old regime


- **Section 123 (previously 80C) and other deductions** : applicable only under the old regime; declared by the employee in Form 124 (previously Form 12BB)


- **Number of remaining months in the financial year** : TDS is spread equally across remaining months from the month of joining


TDS must be recalculated whenever the annual income projection changes: after a bonus payment, a salary revision, or a mid-year change in declaration. If TDS is not recalculated, the year-end shortfall is recovered from the final month’s salary, creating a large unexpected deduction for the employee.


## **Step 5: Set Up Your Payroll System**


Once registrations, salary structures, and employee data are in place, the payroll system needs to be configured before the first run. For a new company, this means:


- **Entering company details:** company name, PAN, TAN, establishment codes (PF and ESI), and state PT registration numbers


- **Configuring salary structures:** defining each component, its calculation method (fixed, percentage of basic, or formula-based), and its taxability


- **Adding employee records:** salary details, joining date, work location, PAN, UAN, and tax regime


- **Setting up leave and attendance:** connecting with your attendance system or setting manual inputs for leave and loss of pay


- **Configuring statutory rules:** PF applicability threshold, ESI gross salary limit (₹21,000), PT slabs per work location, and TAN for TDS


- **Setting up bank disbursement:** either direct disbursal from the payroll platform or generating a bank file for upload


A payroll system that applies PT rules automatically per employee work location means you add each new state once, and its PT rules are applied to every employee working there. This is the step where platform choice has the most long-term operational impact.


## **Step 6: Run Your First Payroll**


The first payroll run for a new company typically involves:


1. **Input verification:** confirm that salary structures, leave inputs, and attendance data are correct before the run begins


2. **Payroll processing:** the system calculates gross pay, statutory deductions (PF, ESI, PT, TDS), and net pay for each employee


3. **Output review:** review payslips and statutory calculations for a sample of employees before disbursing, to catch errors before money moves


4. **Salary disbursal:** credit net salaries to employee bank accounts


5. **Statutory payments:** pay PF (by the 15th), ESI (by the 15th), TDS (by the 7th of the following month), and PT (by the state deadline)


6. **Return filing:** file the monthly PF ECR, ESI return, and the quarterly TDS return when due


7. **Payslip distribution:** share payslips with employees through a self-service portal or by email


Getting the first payroll run right matters beyond accuracy. Employees form an impression of payroll reliability from the first month. A late salary, an incorrect deduction, or a missing payslip in the first cycle creates a credibility problem that takes several correct months to recover.


## **Payroll Setup for Startups: What to Get Right from the Beginning**


For startups setting up payroll for the first time, three decisions have an outsized impact on how payroll scales:


**Register for PF and ESI before you need to, not when you cross the threshold.** Many startups hire contractors and consultants in the early months, then convert some to full-time employees. If PF and ESI registration happens reactively, after crossing 20 employees for PF or 10 for ESI, there is a window where payroll has been processed without the correct deductions. Registering early removes this exposure.


**Build salary structures that hold up at scale.** A salary structure designed for five employees often creates problems at fifty. Components that made sense early become difficult to administer across multiple grades and locations. Building a structured component framework from the start (basic, HRA, special allowance, variable pay) with clear rules for each is easier than redesigning structures after payroll history has accumulated. With RazorpayX Payroll, you can create different salary structures for each department, location or grade, and assign the right one to each employee.


**Choose a payroll system that pays and files your compliance as well as calculating it.** A system that calculates PF, ESI, PT, and TDS correctly but leaves the portal submissions to your team means your finance person is manually logging into EPFO, ESIC, state PT portals, and the income tax portal each month. That manual overhead grows with headcount. A platform that executes compliance payments and files returns automatically keeps that work off your team’s plate as headcount grows.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


**How do I set up payroll for a new company in India?**


Payroll setup for a new company in India involves six steps: register with EPFO, ESIC, the state PT authority, and obtain a TAN for TDS; build your salary structure; collect employee PAN, bank details, UAN, and tax declarations; configure TDS for each employee; set up and configure a payroll system; then run and verify the first payroll. Statutory registrations must be in place before the first payroll run.


**How do I register for PF and ESI as a new company?**


Register for PF on the EPFO Employer Portal (unified.epfindia.gov.in). PF registration is mandatory when you have 20 or more employees, though voluntary registration is available earlier. Register for ESI on the ESIC Employer Portal (esic.in) when you have 10 or more employees earning ₹21,000 or less per month. Both portals issue employer codes that are used for monthly contributions and returns.


**When should a startup register for PF and ESI?**


Startups should register for PF when they reach 20 full-time employees (or earlier voluntarily), and for ESI when they reach 10 employees with any earning ₹21,000 or less per month. Registering before the threshold removes the risk of a compliance gap during a hiring push. Many startups register at incorporation or at the first full-time hire to avoid the complexity of a mid-growth registration.


**What is the PF wage ceiling for new companies in 2026?**


The PF wage ceiling is ₹25,000/month, revised from ₹15,000 effective 17 September 2026. PF contributions are calculated at 12% of applicable PF wages: employee and employer each contribute 12%, with the employer’s contribution split into 3.67% EPF and 8.33% EPS.


**How is TDS on salary calculated for a new employee?**


TDS on salary is calculated by projecting the employee’s annual taxable income based on their salary structure and declared investments, applying the applicable income tax slab, and dividing the resulting tax liability equally across the remaining months of the financial year. Under the new tax regime (the default from FY 2023-24), only a few deductions apply, mainly the ₹75,000 standard deduction and the employer’s NPS contribution. TDS must be recalculated whenever the annual income projection changes.


**How long does it take to set up payroll for a new company in India?**


Statutory registrations (PF, ESI, PT and TAN) are all done online, and timelines vary by state and portal. Payroll system setup (entering company details, salary structures, and employee records) can be completed within a day on modern payroll platforms that support bulk upload and employee self-onboarding.
